result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.antichain_width()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Compute the width of a directed acyclic graph: the size of its largest antichain. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.antichain_width()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Compute the width of a directed acyclic graph: the size of its largest antichain. title: >- [Graph.antichain_width()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Compute the width of a directed acyclic graph: the size of its largest antichain. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the width of a directed acyclic graph: the size of its largest antichain. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L58291-L58362){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.antichain_width() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Antichain width](/assets/graphs/antichain-width.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A DAG drawn left to right: A points to B, C and D; B and C both point to E, and D points to F. B, C and D, in the accent color, cannot reach one another, so they form an antichain of 3 nodes. No larger one exists, because three chains cover the graph, A to B to E, C alone, and D to F, and an antichain holds at most one node of each. The width is 3." width="100%"} An antichain is a set of nodes none of which can reach another along directed paths (see `antichains()`), and the width is the largest such set. In a task dependency graph it is the most tasks that can ever run at once, so it bounds the parallelism any schedule can use; in a version history, the most branches that are ever simultaneously unmerged. By Dilworth's theorem it also equals the fewest chains (sets of nodes all on one directed path) needed to cover every node. Unlike `antichains()`, which lists every antichain and can take exponential time, this runs in polynomial time. Parallel edges count once. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The width (`0` for a graph without nodes). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or has a cycle (including a self-loop). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Fulkerson's (1956) reduction of Dilworth's theorem to matching: build the transitive closure (as bitsets, in reverse topological order), form the bipartite graph joining a left copy of each node `u` to a right copy of every `v` reachable from `u`, and find a maximum matching with Hopcroft-Karp. Each matched pair links two consecutive nodes of a chain, so the fewest chains, and with them the width, is `n` minus the matching's size. The closure takes `O(n e / 64)` time and the matching `O(sqrt(n) r)`, where `r` is the number of reachable pairs. This is how NetworkX's `antichain_width()` computes it, and the results match. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a diamond A -> B, A -> C, B -> D, C -> D, the largest antichain is {B, C}: ::: {#3cb0145d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D")]) g.antichain_width() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: The width of the divisibility order on 1 to 30 is 15, the numbers 16 to 30, none of which divides another: ::: {#f01553bd .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} div = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes([str(i) for i in range(1, 31)]) div.add_edges( [(str(a), str(b)) for a in range(1, 31) for b in range(2 * a, 31, a)] ) div.antichain_width() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 15 ``` ::: :::
